drafted_from: workflow:connect-every-ai-to-one-memory-list's row in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (its input schema, steps and submit shapes)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:connect-every-ai-to-one-memory-list with list_id ai-memories, copy folder /memories, for claude-code and claude-web."

lists.label: AI memories
lists.holds: One thing one AI remembers: its name, who wrote it, what it is about, its text and when it changed.

values.document_text: Lead with the outcome in one sentence, then only the facts that matter.
Sunrise Bakery opens at 6 AM Monday to Saturday.

alike: an AI memory file per assistant

instructions: 1. Pour the example memories into the list where you keep AI memories (see pour), or let the first step make list:ai-memories.
2. Say "Run workflow:connect-every-ai-to-one-memory-list" with list_id, copy_root, copy_folder, public_door, local_door and the ais to connect.

3. The AI works the-list, computer-door, harness-hooks, web-chats, phones, services, copies and proof: one list is the original, a folder on your computer is its copy, each AI that writes files gets a hook, and web chats connect through the public door with sign-in.
4. Read the proof step: a memory one AI wrote must be read by another, appear in the folder, and a change in the file must reach the list; the test memory is then removed.

worked_examples.title: A memory written in a web chat is read by the computer AI
worked_examples.ask: Prove my AIs share one memory list.
worked_examples.given: claude-web writes the memory "memory list check" (document.text "TEST: written by claude-web at 18:20; remove after the check"); claude-code reads it with records:list; the full sync puts it in the file /srv/example-notes/memories/claude-web/memory-list-check.md; one word is changed in that file and reaches the row; the row is then removed. Read from the proof step of the workflow row.
worked_examples.hands_back: The submit shape of step proof: {"writer":"claude-web","reader":"claude-code","both":["claude-web","claude-code"],"file":"/srv/example-notes/memories/claude-web/memory-list-check.md","file_matched":true,"change_reached_list":true,"removed":true}

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
